source: ADR-0071's re-founding table, 2026-08-11 (#326), as amended by ADR-0073, 2026-08-18 (#406). #326 re-founded, class by class, the table the human ruling on #258, 2026-08-06 as amended by #217 item 9, had established. This file carried that pre-#326 table frozen beside the re-founded one for one transition window, so that a process which had not fetched could still read a document its parser understood; the window closed by the human's ruling of 2026-08-14 and #365 deleted the frozen half on 2026-08-16. There is one document here now — routing_classes, routing_issue_exceptions and routing_route_exceptions — and a parser that cannot read it is a parser predating #326 whose worktree needs to rebase. ADR-0073 retires the last lane-selected refusal this table held, class 6's keep-on-Claude bar, on the human's instruction of 2026-08-18, and replaces it with a cross-lane requirement on the review that clears a class-6 landing. **No row in this table refuses any route by lane any more.** What still refuses at dispatch is seating — classes 2 and 3, on every lane including Claude's — and what refuses at landing is the never-alone rung in `tools/land_review.py`, which is not this table's own rung and reads class 6's path list as data.
coverage: This table is not a complete account of what needs routing, and this sentence rides on a clear read as well as on a refusal, because the reader told nothing is wrong is the reader forming a belief about what was checked. Class 6's invariant is enforced since ADR-0073 (#406), but only over the paths it names, and that list is a minority of the gates this project runs; classes 4 and 5 refuse no route at all; classes 2 and 3 are bound to seats and so are checked at dispatch only, since a landing has no seat to check. Since ADR-0073 no row here refuses a landing at all, so the landing's own routing rung can now only refuse an unreadable policy or an unreadable diff, and a `routing=clear` line there means less than it did: it means no row matched, not that any row could have. A surface this file does not name is uncovered, never cleared, and a rung that did not run is not a rung that passed. Class ids 1 and 7 are retired by ADR-0071's re-founding table and are never reused, so an id is a stable historical handle rather than a position.

routing_classes.name: orchestration
routing_classes.label: Orchestration
routing_classes.remedy: Orchestration work goes to its route, and this row is founded on that route's seats rather than on a lane — a row admits the whole route, not its first step, the rule `tools/routing_policy.py` states over class 3 and #327's round 3 applied here: an issue declaring `Routing-class: orchestration` is refused taken by any seat outside the route that finishes that work, on every lane including Claude's. The route is `orchestrator`, which performs the act; `planner`, which plans it; `implementer`, which lands it (ruling 2 — the planner neither gates nor lands); `review`, which reviews that landing (ruling 4 — no change lands alone); and `recon`, admitted on #326 review round 3 claim 4's ground — a seat that authors, lands and reviews nothing cannot take the work, so refusing it protects nothing while barring a cheap read-only sweep. #327's second round appointed `orchestrator` alone and its third widened it (#327 review round 3, claim 1): the one-seat row left an orchestration issue plannable by nobody, landable by nobody, reviewable by nobody — ruling 4's reviewing instance was refused on every lane — and reconnoitrable by nobody, so #331, filed with this very marker, could have been dispatched only to the one seat that must not review its own landing. What the row refuses now is `retro` and `fable` and nothing else — the reading #327 review round 3's caveat asked its fixer to pick, on class 3's own ground, because the row copied does not supply one: both seats can take work and neither is a seat any landed ruling requires for this route, so the refusal still selects, where refusing `recon` selected nothing. That thinness is named rather than hidden: two seats left outside is evidence that the keep-on-Claude half was always the seat table's carve-out. #327 review round 3 recommended putting to the human whether the row should instead be widened further or deleted outright, and **that question is answered rather than open**: the human ruled on 2026-08-14 (recorded in full on #327, filed as #368, landed as ADR-0071 amendment A2 at `ec369b3`) that the ADR is amended and the code stays as landed, with both alternatives — widening further, deleting outright — put and declined. Re-litigating either needs a fresh ruling, not this sentence. **Resolved by #329 (flagged by #327's re-review of round 3, claim 3): `AGENTS.md`'s Model roles paragraph used to send "process docs" to a `fable` seat, and `docs/agents/orchestration.md` — the orchestration seat's operating rules, by `AGENTS.md`'s own Orchestration seat section — is a process doc this row refuses to route there. The sentence was stale rather than the row wrong, and #329 replaced that paragraph with the Seats and profiles section, which routes by seat and no longer sends any surface to `fable` on provenance grounds. The retro half of the same overlap is #330's.** The keep-on-Claude half is not this row's — it is the seat table's carve-out (`orchestrator_claude_only` in `tools/dispatch.py`), the one provenance rule ADR-0071 ruling 1 left standing, provisional until the Codex orchestrator backup is built. Until #327's second round this row carried that half as a lane-selected refusal, which refused every seat on every non-Claude lane for an orchestration declaration while clearing the same declaration on Claude — broader than the carve-out it descended from, because the row was selected by lane and nothing on it narrowed that to a seat. `required_seats` is the mechanism that scopes, so the row uses it. Checked at dispatch only, because a landing has no seat to check — this row carries no `landing_path_prefixes` for the same reason the ADR-authorship row carries none, and `parse_policy` refuses a seat-bound row that does, rather than letting the landing rung silently re-derive the lane bar. **The departure this row once carried is closed (#327 review round 2, claim 1): ADR-0071's re-founding table used to say this row "survives unchanged", which it did not — re-founding it on the route's seats is the fix that review directed, because the alternative was a second lane-selected provenance refusal the landing's prose had counted away. Amendment A2 (`ec369b3`, human ruling 2026-08-14) rewrote that row to "survives, re-founded on the route's seats", so the ADR now describes this row and no ADR-0013 record is owed.**

routing_classes.name: adr_authorship
routing_classes.label: ADR authorship
routing_classes.remedy: Route ADR authorship to the three seats ADR-0071 rulings 2 and 4 require between them, on any lane including a non-Claude one: `planner` authors it, off the ordered profile preferences ruling 2 gives that seat; `implementer` lands it, because ruling 2's planner "neither gates nor lands"; and `review` reviews that landing, because ruling 4 lands no change alone. A row admitting the planner alone admitted nobody who could finish the work and refused the very review dispatch ruling 4 mandates — the deadlock found in #326 review round 2, claim 1 — so the admitted set is the whole route rather than its first step. `recon` is admitted beside those three and is not one of them (#326 review round 3, claim 4): it is read-only by description in `tools/dispatch.py`'s `SEATS`, so it authors, lands and reviews nothing, and refusing it defeats no purpose of a class that exists to stop an ADR being authored from a seat that cannot author one — the round that refused it applied the sufficiency rule ("admit every seat some ruling requires") as a necessity rule, which turns a capability requirement into a bar and routes a cheap read-only sweep to a seat that gates and lands. Its read-only standing was a description and not an enforced `permission_mode` when this row was written, so the admission rested on what the seat is for; #407 closed that gap after a dispatched `recon` session edited `tools/` and its tests, and the seat now forces `plan` in `SEATS` the way `review` does. The admission still rests on what the seat is for — the enforcement is what makes that ground hold rather than a second reason for it — and a `recon` seat that lost the forced mode would need this row revisited. Refused on every lane including Claude's: `orchestrator` is class 2's seat, `fable` is none of the seats rulings 2 and 4 require for this route — the #300 retro allowance that once carried it to ADR work was superseded by ADR-0071's trailer and deleted with the ladder it suspended (#327), so what refuses it here is seating and not provenance — and `retro` files and lands nothing but its own journal under ruling 3 as amended by A4 — the retro half of the class this row descends from is withdrawn by that ruling, along with its `docs/process-log.md` path, and A4 then re-establishes exactly one retro landing on that path, the journal entry, reviewed under ruling 4 like any other landing. This row neither refuses nor clears that landing, and the distinction is worth reading rather than inferring: what this class refuses `retro` is **authoring an ADR**, never journalling, and a seat-bound row carries no `landing_path_prefixes` at all, so no rung here meets `docs/process-log.md` in either direction. **Resolved by #329 (flagged by #326's review round 3, claim 5): `AGENTS.md`'s Model roles paragraph — the file an agent actually reads before dispatching, and `CLAUDE.md` is the committed symlink to it — used to send "anything touching ADRs" to a `fable` seat, which this row refuses.** ADR-0071 ruling 2 superseded that mapping in substance, so the sentence was stale rather than this row wrong; #329 replaced it with the Seats and profiles section, whose `fable` entry is the #181 shape and nothing wider. The retro half of the same overlap is #330's. That is what ruling 1 means by eligibility ceasing to be a property of provenance — a lane-selected refusal here would have refused `codex`/`codex-sol-xhigh`/`planner`, the first entry in the list this remedy prescribes, while clearing any Claude seat whatever. The class is therefore enforced where a seat exists, which is dispatch. `just land` is handed a lane and a diff and no seat, so this row carries no landing prefixes and the landing rung does not test it — an ADR reaching `origin/main` from an unappointed seat is uncaught, not cleared. **Two departures from ADR-0071's re-founding table, both labelled (#326 review round 2, claim 3; #326 review round 3, claim 9).** The first is a conflict: ADR-0071's re-founding table prescribes `docs/adr/` as this row's landing path and this row has none, because a seat-bound row carrying landing prefixes would clear at dispatch for the seat it appoints and then refuse that same route at landing, where no seat is knowable, so the two cannot both hold as written; whether the ADR is amended or an ADR-0013 record covers it is the human's. The second is a synthesis rather than a conflict, and is named so a reader auditing this row against the ADR is not left to spot it: the table binds this class "to the planner's list rather than to Claude", and this row admits four seats. Read literally that is the deadlock — the planner neither gates nor lands — so the row is read together with rulings 2 and 4, whose seats it names above. A reader who thinks the literal words should have won has the departure in front of them rather than buried in a commit message.

routing_classes.name: plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green
routing_classes.label: The #181 shape
issue_phrases: plausible wrong fix would also have gone green
plausible wrong fix would also go green
routing_classes.remedy: No mechanical gate distinguishes this diagnosis's plausible wrong fix from the right one, so the remedy is capability rather than provenance: route it to the `planner` seat and escalate. ADR-0071 ruling 5's fourth transferring-escalation condition, `plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green`, fires on exactly this class and names the transfer; the condition and its remedy are data in `config/escalation-conditions.json` and reach an agent as an emission.

routing_classes.name: in_world_landings
routing_classes.label: In-world landings
routing_classes.remedy: A subagent cannot hold the full `just regress` corpus's foreground wait — `.claude/hooks/deny-subagent-waits.py` denies it — so a seat reached as a subagent cannot gate its own in-world work and must not take it. That is the whole of the rule: `just dispatch` launches a top-level session, which the wait hook permits by returning 0 where there is no agent id, so this row refuses no dispatch route. Its two path lists remain the one authority for what an in-world surface is, read by `just land`'s corpus rung and by `tools/gate.py`, which since #328 is where the derived list lives and which `tools/brief.py` and `tools/trial.py` both call (#302).

routing_classes.name: gates_themselves
routing_classes.label: The gates themselves
routing_classes.remedy: One rule lives on this row now, and it is the **invariant**: no instance authors the gate that judges it. It binds every instance, Claude's included, and since ADR-0073 (#406) a refusal enforces it. This row therefore refuses **nothing at dispatch and nothing at landing**, which is what `refuses: false` says: a `codex` or a `zai` dispatch naming these paths is admitted exactly as a `claude-native` one is, and so is a `just land` from any lane. If you were expecting to be refused here by lane, you are reading a pre-#406 memory of this row. The bar that did that — a non-Claude lane refused these paths, the Claude lane exempt — was provenance and not protection: it exempted the lane that authors nearly every gate change, which is the surface most at risk, and this row conceded in as many words that a Claude landing here had cleared nothing. The human instructed its retirement on 2026-08-18 ('Codex only being allowed to take read only work was definitely not my intent. It should be a full peer to the Claude on CC and Zai on CC paths, subject to model appropriateness rules'), and ADR-0073 records that as the human's own decision rather than a delegated one. What replaces it is the rung named next; the two did not overlap, and #389's question — whether the bar survived deliberately or was forgotten — is answered by that ruling rather than by this sentence. **The rung that enforces the invariant is `tools/land_review.py`'s never-alone rung**, the one ADR-0071 ruling 4 already runs on every landing (#334, #398). Where a landing's diff touches a path below, the verdict clearing it must come from a **different lane** than the author's, not merely a different profile: `review_same_lane` is the refusal, and its remedy names `just dispatch --seat review --reviewing <profile> --lane <lane> --profile <profile>`. Same-provider models share failure modes, which is the argument ruling 4 already makes for never-alone; on the gates themselves it is worth spending one predicate on. Where the author's lane or the reviewer's cannot be placed in `tools/dispatch.py`'s registry the rung refuses `review_lane_unknown`, and where the policy or the diff could not be read it refuses `gate_class_undetermined` — a check that could not run is not a check that passed (#41). The author set is the potential-author set `dispatch.potential_authors` reads plus any profile `just review-loop author` declared, so a lane any record places on the work is excluded whether or not that dispatch wrote a line: over-excluding costs a resolution step and under-excluding costs the invariant. A diff touching one of these paths is also **not** exemptible by `config/review-exemptions.json`: the rung determines the gate paths before it consults that table, on this row's own ground. The path list below is therefore the **one authority** for what a gate path is, the position class 5's list holds for in-world surfaces (#302), and `parse_policy` refuses this row an empty one — a row that emptied would compute 'nothing is a gate' and clear every same-lane review in silence. This class still carries **no exception**, and `binds_every_instance` still enforces that: an instance that can except itself from the gate that judges it is precisely the shape being forbidden, which is also why the `Routing-exception: proposal-only` marker went with the framing. `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/settings.json` are here, not dropped: they are the denial layer and the permission allowlist, and the withdrawn gated-semantic-surfaces class was the only routing rule that named them. Coverage is incomplete, and the new rung inherits exactly this list's coverage and no more: the list names six tools plus those two paths — six since `tools/land_review.py` joined it below — and omits `tools/check_adr_form.py`, `tools/check_seat_config.py`, `tools/check_validated_markers.py`, `tools/check_conflict_markers.py`, `tools/check_source_symlink.py`, `tools/check_sqf_bans.py`, `tools/generate_seats.py` and `tools/export_command_schema.py` — the eight `just check` reaches — and `tools/breaker.py`, which no `check-*` recipe runs and which `just breaker` and `just watch-report` reach instead (review round 2 claim 4, correcting both this clause and ADR-0071's own row 6, which made the same slip), and `tools/trial.py`, which was on this list as `tools/admission.py` and left it with the bar #328 dropped — it gates nothing now and `just watch-report` is the only recipe that reaches it, which is `tools/breaker.py`'s position exactly — along with every gate reached only through `just unit`, `just mutation`, `just land` and `just regress`. One path **joins** the list with ADR-0073 rather than being named as missing from it: `tools/land_review.py`, the rung this row now points at, because a row that names its own enforcement and then leaves that enforcement outside its coverage is the self-exemption the class exists to forbid. Its neighbours `tools/review_loop.py` and `tools/review_exchange.py` are not added here — they are records and readers rather than the rung, and widening the list further is the coverage question ADR-0071 filed and this ruling does not answer. A diff touching a gate this list does not name is uncovered, never cleared.
